status: 2026-11-07, CPU only, fx 757bdb9 (sources hash-checked: 717 files identical), Zig 0.17.0, wabt 1.0.42
units: RV32 instructions retired in rv32emu; turn = session/prompt sent to its response

p0.label: P0 baseline: ReleaseSmall wasm, wasm2c, clang -Os, unaligned scalar access, configured Chat Completions provider, one SSE event per token

gateway.label: + fx's built-in AI Gateway route instead of FX_CONFIGURED_PROVIDERS
gateway.verdict: exact fx code, same semantics; config picks fx's default provider route (gateway serializer and Vercel-protocol SSE reducer instead of the Chat Completions ones)

event.label: + the whole model reply as one SSE event
event.verdict: exact fx code, same semantics; the model server's chunking

chunk.label: + that event in one network read
chunk.verdict: exact fx code, same semantics; transport chunking

clock.label: + frozen virtual clock
clock.verdict: exact fx code, same semantics; OS clock (deterministic)

fast.label: + ReleaseFast wasm (Zig build mode)
fast.verdict: exact fx code, same semantics; build flag (both modes drop safety checks)

i_event.label: P0 + one SSE event per reply only

i_chunk_only.label: P0 + token events in one read

i_aligned_p0.label: P0 on an aligned-only CPU, no hints (P0's 60.4M build)

i_tools1.label: P0 tool set cut to read_file (turn 2 only is comparable)
i_tools1.verdict: changes fx's behaviour (fewer tools); turn 1's tool calls then fail

zbb.label: + Zbb + Zbs (ISA extension)
zbb.verdict: exact fx code, same semantics; CPU extension (costs circuit)

i_aligned_bytes_fast.label: final stack but under-aligned accesses as byte ops (no address check)

native.label: best honest stack + fx's own read/edit/write tools in the guest
native.verdict: changes which fx code runs, toward more of it: fx's native read/edit/write run on the CPU (platform libc/std patched for WASI permissions); grep/glob stay host tools

fast_split.label: same, built as 96 wasm2c files + ThinLTO (the pipeline -O2 needs; clang runs out of memory on one 47 MB file)
fast_split.verdict: exact fx code, same semantics; build pipeline

o2.label: + clang -O2
o2.verdict: exact fx code, same semantics; C compiler flag

base0.label: + wasm linear memory at address 0
base0.verdict: exact fx code, same semantics; wasm2c runtime layout

aligned.label: aligned-only CPU: memargs' alignment hints honoured, under-aligned accesses checked
aligned.verdict: exact fx code, same semantics; wasm2c patch (alignment hints); no misaligned access left

fastcopy.label: + word-at-a-time memcpy/memmove in the runtime for any alignment
fastcopy.verdict: exact fx code, same semantics; platform libc routine (wasm memory.copy)

i_aligned_bytes.label: P0 on an aligned-only CPU, hints honoured, under-aligned = byte ops

native_p0.label: P0 + fx's own read/edit/write tools in the guest

i_o3.label: final stack (row 12) at clang -O3 instead of -O2

groups.group: token estimate (incl. prompt_context.measureProviderRequest, where it is inlined)

build_notes.o2_crash_cause: LLVM ERROR: out of memory (C: nearly full so the page file cannot grow; other jobs hold ~3 GB). Fix: wasm2c --num-outputs=96, the largest function in its own file compiled alone first, ThinLTO across the files.
build_notes.header_bug_found: split files #include "fxcore-impl.h" by quotes, which resolves next to the .c before -I: the unpatched header (bounds checks on) made the first split builds ~2x slower; build.py now patches c/fxcore-impl.h in place.
build_notes.o3: identical instruction count to -O2 under ThinLTO
